walkthroughs.h2: How much carbon do forests store?
walkthroughs.body_html: Tropical forests store around 250 tonnes of carbon per hectare in biomass and soils. Temperate forests store about 150 t/ha. Globally forests hold roughly 860 billion tonnes of carbon, more than the atmosphere. Clearing one hectare of tropical forest can release around 900 t CO2, equivalent to driving an average car for 4 million km.

Deforestation rate = area lost / time. The Amazon lost around 11,000 km2 in 2022. Globally tropical forests lose around 10 million hectares per year, roughly the area of Iceland. Satellite data from Global Forest Watch now tracks change in near real-time, helping prioritise enforcement and restoration.

Reforestation can sequester around 3 to 7 t CO2 per hectare per year for fast-growing tropical species during the first decades. Restoring 350 million hectares globally by 2030 (Bonn Challenge) could remove around 1.7 billion t CO2 per year. Restored forests, however, store less carbon than primary forest and take decades to mature.

mcqs.q: Why is a cold winter not evidence against climate change?
options: Climate refers to long-term averages, not individual weather events.
They reflect sunlight back to Earth.
Cold winters are caused by warming.
It is evidence - if it gets cold sometimes, warming must be wrong.

mcqs.q: Why is burning fossil fuels considered to disrupt the carbon cycle?
options: It creates new carbon that did not exist before.
It releases carbon stored for millions of years much faster than the cycle can absorb.
It removes carbon permanently.
Cold winters are caused by warming.

mcqs.q: How do greenhouse gases warm Earth?
options: It removes carbon permanently.
They block heat from escaping into space (like a literal lid).
They reflect sunlight back to Earth.
They absorb infrared radiation emitted by Earth's surface and re-radiate some back down.
